{=0FIbRZsi}You can not help but notice how people are put at ease by {?PLAYER_CHILD}your {?CHILD.GENDER}daughter{?}son{\?}{?}the {?CHILD.GENDER}girl{?}boy{\?}{\?} and seek {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} company.
{=2s6cH2kE}Even the finest swordsman can perish if his lord is ignorant of the difference between necessary risks and reckless, unnecessary ones.

{=3lDTSlpU}Even the most skilled swordsman or the strongest axe-wielder is to a lancer as the rabbit is to the eagle.
{=6EaKsRtu}Accidents are inevitable, and {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child isn't bothered by the sight of blood. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} acts quickly to staunch bleeding and prevent infection.
{=78dta9Ys}You told {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} that it is cheaper, safer and wiser to win a battle without fighting, if it is possible to do so.

{=7P3wiojT}a sharp mind.
{=8mk6gwvh}You told {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} that a good eye can spot dangers from afar, and a steady hand can take them down before they get close.
{=GARAmzFT}To thrive you must learn to travel faster, work longer, and fight harder than anyone who stands against you.

{=JHMHcZEp}You have seen many marvels on your travels and heard of many more, and one day, you believe, the philosophers of science will rule the world.
{=LEoZ2DV5}a good eye and a steady hand.
{=LUro3Sqr}While spending time with {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child, you notice that {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} shows real ability in {RANDOM_OUTCOME}.

{=QbwNmxrn}You told {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} that skill and brains are all very well, but in many situations there is no substitute for sheer brute might.
{=Rmbd2OkI}You are usually away from your estate, but when you are able to spend time with {CHILD.NAME}, you encouraged {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} to develop...
{=T3vJp4PG}Whoever grasps how prices work can pluck silver out of thin air.

{=ePNba38W}Armies win battles, but farms and towns win wars.
{=jqstr7ZL}Learn to fire men's pride, stoke their anger and dispel their fears, and they will turn from men into lions who will do anything for you.

{=3O1Pg3Ie}At {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} 14th birthday you gave {CHILD.NAME} a special present. You have seen {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} treasure it and believe it will shape who {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} is. You gave {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?}...
{=3hFT34l1}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child helps out the local physician, binding and cleaning wounds and, when the master is absent, prescribing remedies.
{=43zzbI1J}enemy incursions
{=6WUaFzlv}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child forged a sword - blade, hilt and pommel. The artisan said that he has never seen such dedication and patience in one so young.
{=7JoiyH1Y}You heard that {CHILD.NAME} could put an arrow through an arm ring from 100 paces away, but you didn't believe it until you saw it.
{=7mbE4z2v}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} won a friendly horse racing competition, and was rewarded with a magnificent saddle.
{=AaahFmxv}War was never too far away. On more than one occasion, {CHILD.NAME} spotted foes on the horizon and needed to ride away as quickly as possible.
{=BYadInfL}a well-balanced sword.

{=DfbYtRyj}You had second thoughts about giving {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child such a spirited animal, but {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} lept upon its back and galloped like the wind across your pastures.
{=EP0gEG0L}win a race.
{=GOt2uRcJ}In adolescence, {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} began to take on serious responsibilities and compete with adults as a near-equal. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} managed to...
{=IMaTTgPJ}defeat {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} fencing instructor.
{=Jc1YXXjN}an influx of wild beasts
{=K31F1yPI}When you pick up this blade you can almost feel it dance in your hand. Its edge can cut through a stout poll or a human hair drifting on the wind.

{=MX7toYav}{CHILD.NAME} joined a hunting pursuit in pursuit of a pack of wolves who had been ravaging the local livestock. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} tracked and took down one of the beasts with an arrow.
{=R7A3aPwi}A neighboring noble's brutish son took an interest in persecuting {CHILD.NAME}, but the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} gave him reason to look elsewhere for his prey.

{=S3RZLOsv}You can sense the power in the laminated sinews and wood of this weapon. It was made for the calloused hands of a veteran archer and {CHILD.NAME} may need years to be able to fully draw it back, but you know {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} will be motivated to master it.
{=UpgqdJC0}a trip to your realm's court.
{=aiBQo2MR}an outbreak of unrest

{=bTj16PqR}Every well-born youth wants to see the center of it all, where the lords and ladies gather in splendor to converse and connive. You invited the child to see the spectacle first hand, and provided the elegant clothes {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?}'d need to be part of it.
{=bX841Jau}learn the arts of healing.
{=bwYRMGIN}a treatise on siegecraft.
{=cnbeJh6Y}After many tries {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} successfully beat {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} tutor, fair and square, during sparring.
{=cr2jmYxg}You remember poring over the hand-drawn schematics of mangonels and towers for hours, imagining that one day you might build one of these awesome instruments of destruction yourself.
{=fzxJZZEH}Each piece is a work of art. Even without an opponent one could set it up and gaze upon it for hours, contemplating moves and counter-moves.
{=gHgUwteP}natural disasters
{=iMtCbEb3}a finely carved gameboard.

{=jukOfT2Z}Outside events also intruded on {CHILD.NAME}'s adolescence. You believe {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} was particularly shaped by {RANDOM_OUTCOME}. This event increased {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} skills in {SKILL_1} and {SKILL_2}.
{=kAtxHSu9}A great illness swept through your lands. Your child applied what {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} had read in books on nursing fevers and isolating the sick to minimize deaths on your estate.
{=ksXTQXOX}craft a weapon.
{=l5aOTKUi}a magnificent steed.
{=lDMrl7sd}Your district saw more than its share of floods and fires, and {CHILD.NAME} joined in the effort to stem the destruction and rebuild afterwards.
{=ltbU06Fi}become a crack shot.
{=mzu6exTe}an outbreak of plague

{=oaXAY8bw}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child asked to borrow money to trade with a passing caravan. You figure {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?}'d be sharped and learn a lesson, but in fact the {?CHILD.GENDER}girl{?}boy{\?} secured a very lucrative deal.
{=ocl6ECmt}a well-tempered bow.
{=pHbnAZtt}trade like a veteran merchant.
{=rcoueCmk}Adolescence
{=y9RcWMbQ}a local rivalry
{=yym5kCG5}After a particularly hard winter your tenants began to murmur about rising up and seizing your granaries. {CHILD.NAME} convinced them to be patient and wait for relief.

{=0CCgjMTG}Cover the bodies as best you can and hope for the best

{=0DSopB7F}After observing the terrain around {FORTRESS_NAME}, you think conditions might be appropriate for mining - digging a tunnel under a wall, then collapsing it. This can open a breach but is time-consuming and risky. If you encounter rock underground, you may find all your efforts go to waste. If the ground is too soft, the tunnel may collapse and bury your men. Most troops are reluctant to spend time in dark, confined tunnels unless they are paid extra, or forced.
{=0EG0iB9p}Rooster theft
{=0Wwwa77J}Tell the trader that you have no wish to profit from his ignorance
{=0ZP5fDBX}Let the wealthier merchant know that your decision is for sale.
{=0avcvATJ}Jobs for the Lads
{=0awbcZag}Give him your blessing and encourage him to bore everyone to tears with his old war stories.
{=0k4T7dzu}Return the rooster and have your man whipped.
{=0lqAKHfU}Tell your men to be forgiving, as they were once recruits themselves
{=0wRiev5G}Show genuine remorse and participate in the burial rites for the deer, just in case, even if your troops make comments behind your back
{=0xiAZr96}Tell {NOBLE.NAME} that your people will get their reeds elsewhere and stop frightening off the game.
{=0yKJ0J0N}Feeling the Bite
{=12bIzNkB}Tell him that no one sells maps to treasures that they could just as easily dig up themselves
{=12bmA5qD}Speculative Investment
{=1b9oYu6v}Tell them they can join you and be as arrogant as they like - so long as they beat one of your men in a duel to first blood.
{=1bobtmxl}Sell him your cheapest horse so that he can continue.
{=1cgOQB5K}Vintage of Victory

{=1jAyaivZ}As you pass through the village streets, a dog dashes out from among some spectators and bites at the heels of one of your {CAVALRYMAN}'s horses, panicking it. The mount rears and gallops down the street, trampling a vegetable vendor who was unable to get out of its way. She will probably walk with a limp hereafter, and her family demands compensation.
{=1jmYaNxu}Veteran Mentor
{=1zsWhG2N}Tell your men as best you can that, while you respect their spirit, this will frighten local farmers who don't understand warriors' ways.
{=24pUil64}You like that fiery spirit! Let them fight until one falls and cannot rise
{=2GMj6ZaW}Carry the bodies with you until you find dry wood or softer ground

{=2KaXj3Qa}The depredations of the {NEARBY_ENEMY_FACTION} has driven many farmers from their homes. Those who have land usually return to it, but many of the poorer are seeking a new place to live. You speak to a few encamped on the outskirts of your village. There is no land for them. They seem eager to work as tenants, but there is always a possibility of tensions with the more established village families.

{=2OQlwt7x}Villagers say that a wanderer has recently arrived and offered to teach their children to read. He is not only well-educated, but he has a gift for holding the attention of restless 10-year-olds. However, he seems to have spent time with one of the rebel bands that were common around here ten years back, and occasionally speaks of a coming reign of justice brought by Heaven, in a way that doesn't seem like one of his ironic jokes.
{=2auYPXJ8}Declare that you owe your victory to your own right arm, and keep the silver
{=2dW3cBQy}That steel is forged from iron, and long hard marches breed tough warriors.
{=2xvqOUJh}Tell him quietly that you will not profit off of the misery of others.
{=37YTPzfG}Tell your men that they have all earned the right to your esteem, and break out an extra ration of {FOOD_OR_DRINK_ITEM} to show your appreciation
{=37lEhqtv}Let them fight until the first drop of blood is shed
{=3CaDxb8R}Remind your men that war is war, the {TROOP_TYPE} knew the risks, and prisoners bring ransoms

{=3FwbFdbw}As you inspect your siege camp, you come across disgusting evidence that one or more of your men has contracted the bloody flux. It will pass from man to man as they share food and water, and you know what it can do to a besieging army if left unchecked.

{=3IphvZTK}In your absence, several families in your district have been hard at work draining a marsh and turning it into a field. The survey records in your treasury however indicate clearly that the marsh is part of your domain. They almost certainly did not know this, but you are entitled to claim the field or charge them for working it.
{=3M54uDKZ}The Quiet Life
{=3OerG5Ik}Take the teacher aside, and tell him the elder will pay him a handsome stipend that will stop abruptly if he breathes a word about politics or theology.
{=3QobDImA}Help them get back on their feet, even if some will call say that you are too trusting
{=3Uub2e17}Tell your men that there shall be no wine tonight, and none henceforth until they learn how to handle themselves in the desert.
{=3WFuf7OC}Give them money to purchase land near your fief in {VILLAGE_NAME}, so long as they take charge of training the local militia.

{=3eOOT66E}One of your tenants has a proposal for you. He proposes to dig a channel known as a qanah into a hillside, where the water table is high, which will allow him to flood some low-lying ground and turn it into an oasis garden. The barren hillside is your property, though at present it yields no income of any kind.
{=3uHIXyDk}Your men could use a laugh. Let the recruit show off his prize to his mates and take the humiliation, even if it's enough to drive him to desert
{=3zEtGAII}You agree with the ancient Palaic principle: the lands belong to the spirits of the earth, not to humans, and go to those who make the best use of them.
{=3zP80NBJ}Tell them that village disputes are a matter for a proper inquest by the authorities

{=42bGMh4X}Your men were not expecting to spend so much time in the desert. They complain that baggage that they might gladly carry themselves in normal times becomes a crushing burden when the blazing sun is high in the sky. They have located a number of pack animals in the markets and ask you to buy them to lighten their own loads.
{=43GeTG0K}Accept, even if it costs you time, recognizing that a warrior who survived so many battles probably knows a thing or two.
{=47hUs9yg}You make an example of the foreman. You hand him over to the town authorities and encourage them to apply the full penalty - branding as a thief and exile from the town.
{=4Ef7xG1o}Propitiate the spirits as the villagers advised, by slaughtering a black cockerel that they sold one of your men.
{=4WZ5CWm8}Take them aside and tell them that while nihilism is fine for a boozy salon in {TOWN_NAME}, it's a bit much for men who must every day put their lives on the line.
{=4dIYUMkA}Donate the spoils of battle to the saint's shrine
{=4mC7AIPk}Troops Fight over Insult
{=4v8LpVb8}Send some men to fetch a doctor and medicine, accepting that it will delay your march
{=52l7VuWI}Tell her that Heaven expects her to bear her fate with dignity.
{=56hS9BRG}Admonish the {HIGH_TIER_TROOPS} for their indiscipline, even though they will be humiliated and may even desert
{=57VuY9ln}Poison it! Some women and children of {FORTRESS_NAME} may well perish along with the defenders, but such is war.
{=5ByLt1QP}Tell the Sisters that they will slow you down, and your men can heal on their own.
{=5HsJkbZz}You brought your men into their village, and you must take responsibility.
{=5LOG5afj}Ice March

{=5OuDl2Po}As you come into town, the merchant {MERCHANT_NAME} makes you an offer. Local merchants are on edge awaiting an incoming caravan from {PLACE}. If you claim that you found its wreckage, looted by bandits, the prices of goods would rise considerably. He offers to pay you 1000 denars, in addition to whatever extra you can make by selling your own wares once the prices rise.
{=5OzX71s3}Dodgy Spice
{=5SWqBZSh}Demand that your men respect the customs of war and tend to those who gave quarter
{=5aPGeeDf}Spoiled Food Supplies
{=5krpAZu6}Chide them gently for walking off the job before coming to you first, because of course you'll up their wages.
{=5rjUJaW4}Hunting requires patience. You've got real battles to fight.
{=5vN2NZ8R}Nomads Wish to Settle
{=6IA1S2XU}Family Claims Bandit
{=6bF0LqJo}Vedmak's Treasure
{=6sAI5uOm}Tell the village that they must pay the lad's ransom, so that he will know there is no profit in banditry
{=78VrrDRM}Tell them that you believe them to be oathbreakers, and as such have no place in your ranks.
{=7YCEpRij}Reprimand the footman, who you know will grumble but will have the sense to swallow his pride
{=7f06ovrO}Applaud his plan, and tell him that you will charge him nothing to sink a channel through your property.

{=7fpGI4Jb}Shortly after the loot is distributed, you come across several of your men rubbing the edges of the coins that you paid them against a rock. You recognize what they're doing - clipping, or shaving off a bit of the silver to melt down in the hope that no one will notice.
{=7q53TLg7}Wages of war and diseases
{=7y4Fbx8K}A Suitable Boy

{=82Fno8Vr}Your clerk at your {WORKSHOP} in {TOWN} has caught one of your foremen skimming from the funds you use to purchase raw materials. Luckily, he did not take much, and he readily confessed. How do you prevent this from happening in the future?
{=8FobMTCH}Broken-down Wagon
{=8JqCDWRd}Welcome them, and give them a donation to purchase small plots of land.
{=8gEBPabt}Let them go and demand they split their haul with you
{=8gTYsXZM}Continue to send your reed gatherers there, and have them bring staves and slings to defend their rights
{=8jCcqBSV}Distribute the land to some of your veterans as a reward for their service
{=8jG2vlOu}Gold Rush
{=8rEX8rjv}Tell {NOTABLE.NAME} that you will write whatever {?NOTABLE.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} wants, for the proper price.

{=8uabQDxp}Tell her, as soberly as you can, that her husband gave his life for a noble cause. Hand her a purse of 100 denars, and tell her that you are sure that he would be happy if she marries again, as long as he remains in her memory.

{=8zFwYZeQ}As you ride off, a villager runs after you accusing one of your men of stealing a rooster. A few squawks silence the culprit's attempt to deny the crime. Honor requires you to uphold the laws of the land, but your men expect a generous {RANK} to value those who shed blood for {PRONOUN} over those who do not.
{=99w595qn}Haunted Dreams
{=9aYLFpC9}Just hand over the money to make the problem go away.

{=9ab6HwCS}As you prepare to leave the village, the elder approaches you. His nephew is to be married, and it would be a great honor if a warrior of your renown would bless the couple. Your men suppress grins and jostle each other, and you know they are looking forward to the chance to get royally drunk.
{=9e8I99t3}Transfer ownership to the farmers to encourage such enterprise, even if others may take advantage of you in the future.
{=9mHMjIqd}Refuse, knowing that separate rituals will breed suspicion among the different cultures in your ranks
{=9uaAUCas}Singing for Supper
{=9yFSbR36}Whip the responsible cavalryman for his negligence, and let him buy his own remount.
{=9yrWWbHF}Tell the woman that her son shall face the same penalties as any other bandit you caught
{=A4voELZr}Order the disposal of the infected horses to avoid further contamination.
{=ACzeec4e}Agree to purchase the camels.
{=AIABabCI}Kill the horse and the two other horses it shared a stable with.
{=AwBJzppu}Take the horse without paying. Tell the seller that thieves have no right to complain of theft.
{=AxGaZNry}Let him do it and reward him generously, but tell him to describe your losses and faults as well
{=B1cyEaQA}Dreams are but a temporary madness. Heaven does not speak to us in this way.
{=B9HD9PNw}A likely story... Place the man under arrest and send word to the authorities of {TOWN_NAME}, who have the time to sort things out.

{=BG8Ph5La}As you leave {VILLAGE_NAME}, a woman approaches you and grasps your horse's halter. Among your prisoners is her son, she says. You captured him when he was part of a gang of bandits, but she tells you tearfully that he is a good boy who fell in with bad company. She swears she'll ensure that he doesn't stray again from the correct path.

{=Bi8fKaGw}As you leave town, one of your cavalrymen finds his mount lying on the ground, whining in pain and refusing to get up. You're sure that he was careless and fed the animal too quickly after your arrival, as he was eager to get to the town's tavern.
{=BjUtGJg6}Break out your food and allow them to fill their bellies before your depart
{=BslqBNQj}Tell them that you cannot help
{=BxpJKMYq}Dispel the spirits in the approved orthodox Calradian way, by loudly calling on Heaven to ward off the ghosts of Below.

{=CKKIJZcB}Have some of your men boil up a soup. Keep a watchful eye on all the beggars, especially those who move too vigorously to the front of the line, and serve only those who seem genuinely too frail to work.
{=CNYKy7q3}Congratulate the soldier on his wise purchase, and tell him that you expect to see him in the thick of the fray in the next battle

{=CObK3sDa}As you leave the village, a greybeard walks up to you carrying a cudgel. Although he's too old to fight, he says, he was a warrior once and claims to know a trick move, a way of suddenly closing with your opponent and tripping them with a spear, which he offers to teach to your troops for a price. He shows you his battle-scars, which are indeed impressive.
{=CX8WdvvR}Lice and Fleas
{=CXZxDvry}Tell your soldiers they should rely on their own strength instead of magic

{=CZamxmfc}As you pass through the town gates, you are thronged by a group of refugees from the countryside. They are gaunt, with sunken eyes. They say they were unable to sow their fields this year for fear of bandits, and were forced to eat their seed grain. They ask for any scraps you can offer.
{=Cba9zsDh}False Money
{=CyM5bAdB}You're not sure you trust the seller, but you're not handing over to officials who might just hang him and seize the horse themselves. Go on your way.
{=D750cNUH}Turn a blind eye, even though the practice is considered little better than counterfeiting

{=D7ZcX8XR}As you pass through the market, {NOTABLE.NAME} requests a minute of your time. {?NOTABLE.GENDER}Her{?}His{\?} cousin is planning on doing some business in {TOWN}, and {?NOTABLE.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} would like a letter of reference from you. You know next to nothing about the lad, although {NOTABLE.NAME} swears that he is honest and conscientious. You find you are receiving a number of these types of requests as your fame spreads.

{=D9T64ejr}As you leave {VILLAGE_NAME}, several of the villagers approach you. They warn you that stagnant ponds from the last rain have yet to fully dry and have bred mosquitos. They offer to sell you a concoction of oils including rosemary, catmint and other herbs that they say will ward off all flying vermin.
{=DCy85lqp}Apples from Heaven
{=DFIPsN1W}If they come to you in need, it is not for you to question them. Have your men distribute alms as usual.
{=DHcl6JU5}Give him one of your own horses, add the mule to your pack train, and tell him to talk to you before he makes any more purchases
{=DOPdMPla}Upbraid {NOTABLE.NAME} in the street for all to hear for daring to presume that you would recommend anyone that you do not know.
{=DcaV3yt9}Order your men to throw away the spoiled food
{=Dogg1b9a}Take the recruits. Try not to be too hard on them at first, even though they'll probably corrode your party's discipline.
{=E659QFHp}Free meat, a bit of fun and practice for your men. Sound the hunting horn.
{=E8IpjMAw}The bushes may belong to someone. Leave them to the local farmers
{=EAu32UBG}Tell your recruits that your veterans have indeed earned the right to the best food
{=EFUNx0cv}A vat of wine for you to dance in honor of the lady Agalea!
{=EIbmlJRP}Tell the elder he'll need to find some other way to handle his troublemakers.
{=ELXomm1C}Cries in the Mist
{=EM8bWb1b}Demand that your men stop, and inform any merchants in the next town that they should look very carefully at whatever coins your men give them.

{=EbNZg7jp}In hot climes, often the most vulnerable part of a fortress is its water supply. Most depend on wells but those can run dry. After days spent in front of {FORTRESS_NAME}, you've caught glimpses of the defenders slipping into the hills. You explore where they've gone, and eventually you come across a rudimentary cistern. You suspect that they must be refreshing their water here.
{=Edn4syjZ}Indulge your men, even though you have little doubt that the wedding is an invention

{=Eih6lrcN}Business is good at your {WORKSHOP} in {TOWN}, but in the rush to keep up with demand the normal precautions are not being taken. {INJURY_TEXT} He will live, but is unlikely to be able to do skilled work, and the rest of the workers are worried about future accidents.
{=EilA5dlq}Respect for the Slain
{=EyHD7gjy}Say you'll swear up and down that you saw the wreckage, damaging your reputation, but demand 2000 denars instead.
{=EzpB6hJG}Try to play down the image of a madman by being as friendly as possible on your next visit to town.

{=FJzoOKIU}You come across a trader whose wagon has gotten stuck in the road after his draught horse went lame. He is desperate to sell his wares before they spoil, and offers them at a bargain price.

{=FKkG15p7}As you leave the village, a trader comes up to you and says the "silver" denars that some of your men just gave him are just polished iron. You can indeed see some specks of rust. He demands that you pay him in full. It's entirely possible that your men tried to pass off some false coinage, but the trader's "evidence" could equally easily have come from his own stock.
{=FL8rUSWo}Sorrows of War

{=FPnUWAj1}After the battle, one of your {TROOPS} from your party approaches you, dreamed of riding with your cavalry as a {NOBLE_TIER}. He has the money to buy his own horse, and he certainly distinguished himself in the fight. You know however that this will go down badly - with the high-born cavalry, who prefer to mingle with their own class, but probably even more so with his comrades, who will think he scorns them.
{=FYvrShj3}Servants of Mercy

{=FZXYHC7s}Between the wars and an epidemic, the villages near {FIEF_NAME} are experiencing a shortage of people, especially young men. Fields are going fallow for lack of hands to plough them, especially those cleared only in recent generations where the title is in dispute. As liege, you can redistribute this unused land, but you will need to find labor.
{=Fa0J7a6M}Boar in a Thicket

{=FbKc1AwE}Several of your newer recruits approach you. Your {HIGH_TIER_TROOPS} have been demanding the freshest cuts of meat and highest quality bread from your stores, letting them make do with gristle and stale crusts. The veterans say that this is the privilege of experience, and that it will motivate your recruits to improve themselves.
{=G16Nlaaq}Wedding Celebration
{=G8eaX10B}You treat all your workers as potential thieves, having them searched coming and going from the workshop.
{=GDHHAyQ5}Soldier in Debt
{=GFGuSmN9}Abundance of troublemakers
{=GL0jmbbJ}No Time to Mourn
{=GMQROhTM}Order your troops to give the upstart a sound beating. Who does he think he is, the hero of some foolish romantic poem?
{=GNdltUJj}Desperate Times

{=GTPPtara}March about the camp, searching for specks of rust on swords or sentries who aren't fully attentive to their watch. Give any violators hard, pointless tasks to teach them to keep their standards up.

{=GgYzaakh}Trade in {TOWN_NAME} has been booming, and prices and wages have been going up. The workers at your {WORKSHOP} have taken notice. Your superviser reports that they have all refused to come in to work until they receive a pay increase. He notes that there remain plenty of hungry mouths and willing hands in town, but that the current workers might cause trouble if they are replaced.
{=Gjd6nP29}You will not sully the good name of anyone with an obviously false rumor
{=GpUBP10Q}As you leave the village, a merchant who clearly wants your approval shouts out, "{LOCAL_KING} has slain his thousands, but {PLAYER} his tens of thousands!"
{=Gsazqfhj}Let them test their plan. Buy a hide, sew the men into it with their weapons, and gather the company to watch in amusement as they struggle to free themselves.

{=H7Co1wqC}Two of your {NOBLE_TIER} have lately been causing a stir in the camp with their irreverent religious preaching. They propound that this world is a illusion, created by a being called the Demiurge for its own amusement, and humans are but game-pieces. You think this may be the Marcorionist doctrine, declared heretical by the imperial Senate some years ago. It is clearly disturbing your more traditional-minded troops and is probably also not good for your party's reputation.
{=HG7WWmX8}Punish the troublemakers for sewing mutiny
{=HT1mQuCI}Feast! Thank Heaven and the spirits of the land, and make merry
{=HXVVJYQr}Tell him curtly what he did and that he needs to go get his old mount back from the trader, even if it costs him a few denars
{=HXj3itpQ}Your {TROOP_TYPE} confessed. There is no option but to let the law take its course
{=HZwt5rVy}Keep marching, even though there is a good chance some of your men might be separated.

{=HbOFGhTG}Tragic tales are always the most popular. Ensure the bard does not leave out the daemon who sits on your shoulder, your bouts of madness, and the witch who foretold your terrible but heroic death
{=HbQDtv60}Reprimand the cavalryman, even though he is fiery and might desert

{=fyJ6aDOQ}Burst into a righteous fury and hand out extra punishments, so that no one will ever again dare neglect their equipment

{=gQigaCkD}One of your {RECRUIT} fell asleep on guard. He was new to your company and not popular, and your men are angry. He put their lives at risk, and they demand he be turned over to them to face the ancient Calradic penalty - to run the gauntlet of men with sticks who will beat him, an ordeal that frequently ends in death.
{=gUKUisS6}An Affair of Honor

{=guEjfYhO}One of your {TROOP_NAME} had some drinks with the arena master in {TOWN} and left the tavern with a job offer - work as a trainer and occasional combatant. The signing bonus is generous. He is reluctant to leave you, and you'd be reluctant to lose a valuable soldier, but he'd be in a fine position to sing your praises.
{=gxGlWxVC}Slow down until the stragglers can catch up
{=hewpozXg}Gnostic Boys
{=hj27QkT3}Keep it to sell, telling your men that the money will be spent on keeping them safe
{=hnMUxRyt}Denounce him angrily in public as a food hoarder for all to hear, so that word gets around of your compassion and mercy.
{=htMJ1uiy}Load the sick onto a cart and give them water, but otherwise let their comrades have as little contact with them as possible.

{=i0SwEBdf}Throughout your visit to {VILLAGE}, the villagers were worried that the enemy who sacked {LOOTED_VILLAGE} might be sending patrols their way. As you leave, you find out that their fears were not misplaced. The first thing you see is a flight of ravens in the sky. Your men begin to mutter to themselves, but soon they stumble across a sight that silences them - a pile of burned corpses, stacked by a crossroad, left by the {ENEMY} as their calling card. You press on, but you soon notice that your men are casting an eye towards your prisoners. They may not have been directly involved in what happened in {LOOTED_VILLAGE}, but you doubt your men care much.
{=iB2g7XBt}Insist he purchase the hillside from your at market rate.
{=iR3ZuTSW}Acknowledge him by howling like an animal and swirling your weapon about, as mad behavior makes for good stories.
{=iSZCkpt3}Welcome them with open arms and a small donation to buy plots of land for their homes

{=iV57q3Tm}A strolling minstrel offers to compose an epic ballad about your heroic deeds, potentially increasing your renown for a little amount of coin. Do you accept his offer, and if so, do you offer him any guidance on what to sing?
{=iYfbN2yb}Intriguing Rumors
{=iiwhVNBb}You respect the defenders' cunning. Simply observe how they slip out of the fortress, by ropes or hidden gates, and learn from it.
{=irLNaJ3m}Tell your men to give themselves a good scratch and keep marching
{=iuAMSSTY}Mad Dog
{=j0HmgDOA}Maintain your claim to the land, but allow the farmers to make use of it for only a token rent.
{=j8Aq3lRW}Veterans demand privileges

{=jB4tmY9W}As you leave the village, a young woman approaches you carrying a months-old baby, surrounded by her relatives. She points at one of your men and says that he was the father, and that he should stay here and wed her. The lad, a strong fellow but not good with words, is too flustered to speak. You can't exactly recall if you passed through here a year ago or not.
{=jE9aKaYd}People will believe a noble's former servant. This man's favor is worth a purse of silver to you.

{=jGafCYMe}Villagers from your fief of {VILLAGE} have started going to a marsh on the road to {VILLAGE2} to gather reeds for baskets, supplementing their earnings. Hunters from {VILLAGE2}, owned by {LORD.NAME}, say they've been disturbing the local waterfowl. Neither of you has title to the marsh, but {VILLAGE2} says that its people started going there first. Your tenants say it's not their problem if they've figured out a better way to make use of the resources.
{=jON8A2UY}A bunch of loud amateur hunters will scare the game and probably injure themselves. Let your scout bag an animal or two, while the rest of your party marches ahead.

{=jUBTrdbE}You take a quick look over your men before you ride out, and you are shocked to notice the state of their equipment. In particular, several of the men have frayed bridles and shield straps that look like they might snap in battle. They are supposed to oil and replace their leather at their own expense, and clearly have not been doing so.
{=jUlHTiSU}Agree with the villagers that nomads are more trouble than they are worth.
{=jeWayyGY}A reprieve is fine, but you tack on a bit of interest so that you're not overwhelmed with hard luck stories
{=jwsexTeh}No horseman can control a mount that is under attack from a dog. Refuse.
{=k4aNfNHg}As on the battlefield, so on the workshop floor. Let each team work at its own pace, receiving bonuses for output, but also taking responsibiliy for injuries.
{=k4kbVxTL}Colicky Horses
{=kZJvgtE3}Dismount, burst into tears, take her hands in yours and tell her that every life lost in your service tears at your heart, and that you want nothing more but for these wars to end.
{=kl13BJZB}Turnpike

{=kntd1zYo}Tunnel quickly, threatening to execute anyone who refuses for insubordination
{=l2rWAm4N}Camp Fever
{=l8rpMldr}Occupational Safety
{=lCumAw9j}Rely on the usual methods

{=lFaBQPxk}Your {CULTURE_NAME} troops ask if they can take charge of the {CULTURE_BURIAL_STYLE} of the {CULTURE_NAME} in the enemy's ranks, declaring that they feel a duty to their kin even if they fought in a bad cause.
{=lPAC4x1e}Tell your men to steer clear of such dubious enticements
{=lbSsRg8w}Your men will resent any curbs on their celebrations, even for their own health. Warn them but take no other precautions.

{=lfJ6OHgX}The village has seen an unexpected rise in pregnancies. Some of your villagers ask your permission to hold a festival in honor of Agalea, protectress of motherhood. Agalea has never been recognized as a saint by the imperial Senate, and many consider her veneration to be a primitive Palaic holder. Her festivals tend to be rather raucous, befitting the theme of fertility, and also rather expensive. It would certainly set tongues wagging in the district. Do you grant permission?
{=lfYEujfb}Local Hero
{=lm37mXGH}Let your men return and sack the town while it is still defenseless
{=lnF2ci30}Tell the merchant that once he accepts currency, it is his fault and his responsibility
{=lrysxcAE}A bit of lead never hurt anyone! Try them all, and split the profits with your {TROOP.NAME}.
{=lzK4PmYL}Rob the entertainers. No doubt their wealth is ill-gotten, and to whom will they complain?
{=m35ezdZG}You don't need a bard to recount your heroic deeds
{=m9MbuMlw}Injury Accident
{=mBkCqpEj}Tell your men that they can avenge their comrade as they see fit
{=mEqk8UCG}This region could use more people. Let word get out.

{=mZir8Ogn}As you prepare to leave, the village elder approaches you. There's a gang of four lads who are constantly picking fights with the other villagers, he says. Even their own families don't want them around for fear they'll end up killing someone and cause a blood feud. He begs you to take them into your ranks, where they can learn a bit of discipline.
{=mezu0Pej}Inform the villagers of your discovery
{=mmlk2tXh}The fun is on you! Hurl a fistful of silver at the entertainers and tell them your men deserve nothing but the best
{=msK9baMp}Kannic Splendors
{=n2mOvIPt}You appeal to your men's better natures. You plea for leniency for your foreman, and beg them not to take advantage.
{=n6gqNNJ0}Tell your men to help themselves.
{=naVH8uSO}"Any blood I have shed may have been necessary but I hope that Heaven will forgive me."
{=nbshAaHo}The letter of the contract would favor the wealthier partner. Merchants should be careful what they sign.

{=nuqL3OAF}As you are leaving your fief you stumble across an altercation. A group of nomads, who pass by annually on their migration from summer to winter pastures, have allowed their herds to graze in your tenants' crops. Your troops far outnumber the nomads and your tenants are urging you to teach them a lesson, but of course their kin might retaliate at a later date.

{=nyZpbVbv}Your men are very proud of their leader - perhaps too proud. Every time they go into town, they spread exaggerated tales of your recklessness in battle. You imagine that this could win you a few admiring recruits, but more and more you've caught a look that suggests fear or distrust, as though you're a wild animal or a demon.
{=o4aQ2UEL}Tell them to make their homes someplace else.
{=o5LpNEIa}Fertility Festival
{=o7kYGTjF}Tempting Berries
{=oIknbpZl}Force the recruit to run the gauntlet
{=oL1qlaxH}Explain to him your reservations, even though you can tell he won't like to hear them, and let him make up his own mind
{=oQmuxCSk}Do your best to explain to the girl that marriages are affairs of the head, not of the heart, and she had better think of her future and that of her children and not elope.
{=ocsX04bn}"I am a river of wealth unto you, my brave warriors!"
{=ogP9E5Hx}Reason with the inspector over a splendid dinner and an amphora of the finest wine that is of course on you.

{=oxBlBLWF}You noticed that the deer around this Khuzait village are unusually unafraid of humans. One of your men manages to shoot one. The villagers approach him afterwards and beg him not to eat the animal. Their former shaman transformed himself into a deer some years ago, they say, and while they don't know if the animal your man killed is him or not, they want to perform the burial rights properly, just to be sure.
{=p0bMRIum}Right of Pillage
{=p0gqO74k}Money is tight and you've eaten worse in your time. Tell the lads to think of it as seasoning
{=p8ESONLB}Donative Demand
{=p8yBnCG2}Let your men enjoy their meal, but commend the villagers for making a good attempt to get their hands on a piece of perfectly good meat

{=pNVKWAKo}Throughout your visit to {VILLAGE}, one of your older {TROOP_TYPE} seems moody and downcast. As you march out, he suddenly stops, stares at a roadside stall, then breaks ranks from your party and starts shouting at the vendor. The story quickly comes tumbling out. He served in one of the Empire's old legions in a battle here against the {NEAREST_OTHER_CULTURE}, and the vendor is selling scraps of metal that were clearly looted from the graves of the dead.
{=pjy9Z4bt}Charitable Acts Recognition
{=q0HIXEal}Letter of Reference

{=qBsa5KC5}As you leave town you come across an encampment of traveling entertainers. You see tattered but colorful tents, you hear wailing but enticing music, and smell the scent of cheap incense and meat that is probably slightly spoiled but spiced so that you would never notice. A group of women in some noble's thrown-away silks, their faces made up skillfully with charcoal and sheep's blood, beckon to your men. What do you do?
{=qCoqaa70}Have your men wrap themselves up as best they can and press on.
{=qFa4Oik0}Sleeping Sentry
{=qRZpuLae}End the animal's misery quickly, and tell the horseman that you will not trust another poor beast to his care.

{=qaGbN6wX}It has not escaped your men’s notice that you have accumulated a fair amount of money in your treasury. A delegation approaches you and suggests that this would be a good time for the traditional donative, as Calradian emperors of old were known to give their legions.

{=qljKyPrR}Tell your men that the prisoners must be kept safe and that you will hold them responsible for anything that happens
{=qoSObD62}Tell {ARTISAN_NAME} to do his worst - you're not firing men who've served you well.
{=rG4b9Tft}The Pavillon
{=rRVEjUWH}Show them a few tricks from your rogue's repertoire

{=raLLq10c}Grazing land has grown scarce near {TOWN_OR_CASTLE_NAME}, and a heath between {POORER_VILLAGE} and {RICHER_VILLAGE}, covered with thistle and formerly of little value, has become a point of contention. {POORER_VILLAGE} claims that they have been taking goats there for generations, but {RICHER_VILLAGE} has produced a document showing legal title.
{=rflKyqOT}No Country for the Afflicted

{=rm4ApCIW}Now that the fighting has ended you notice that the weather has turned bitterly cold, and a wind is picking up. Soon after you return to the march, you notice that several of your men have fallen behind. Your men are shivering in the wind, however, and are in no mood to wait. You can march on and hope they catch up to you, or set a slower pace.

{=rpvUQUmq}You've been studying the walls of {FORTRESS_NAME} for days, and you see what appears to be a crack in one place - possibly the result of an old earthquake, or just negligence. It's hard to hit with your catapults and the ground is too rocky to mine, but you reckon troops with pickaxes by themselves could bring it down - assuming they were willing to brave the storm of arrows and rocks that would no doubt come pouring from the battlements above.

{=sQA7Z3Pp}As you set out from the village, a local hunter tells you that he can lead you to a nest made by a particularly large boar in a nearby thicket. The animal is a threat to the village and too fierce for him, he says. It already killed two of his dogs. Your men could probably get it and claim a meal of fresh pork, though not without risk.

{=sU4t3v9r}A passing trader offers to buy {GOOD} from your party at well over the price that it would fetch in the nearest town. No doubt some other merchant has fed him bad information on prices, either to put a rival out of business or as a joke.
{=sb9zWc3I}Give your blessing to the marriage and hurl huge handfuls of coins to the villagers, declaring that this will be a day that all shall remember.
{=ssAwOnse}Grant their request, as there is no shame in honoring a valiant foe
{=sxH5NHba}"I have, and it is but an appetite-whetter before the main meal."
{=sxrBpIUk}Have I killed without good reason? Heaven wishes me to repent! I shall choose the peaceful path. When there is one, that is...

{=t0iKT1VJ}As the dust of battle settles, you see a group of women tending to the wounded. They explain that they are the Servants of Hope, mendicant sisters pledged to assist the afflicted in the hope of winning mercy from Heaven. They offer to accompany your party for a few days and tend to your men's wounds, asking nothing in return.
{=tDK8b1J8}You vaguely recall hearing that lead might be poisonous, but you'll try the others.
{=tGwbM59L}Market Manipulation
{=tK6IkgCK}Tell your men that Heaven expects them to show mercy to the innocent
{=taVbaFFW}Sternly instruct them to respect the traditions of settled life, even though the cold welcome might scare some away
{=te1A19Xe}Tell your {CAVALRYMAN} that he can sort it out.

{=tfckGAIA}As you prepare to leave, one of your men says the he was approached by a villager. There is a particularly ill-tempered vedmak on the edge of town who makes his living not from healing or love-potions but from black magic, and who threatens to curse villagers unless they pay him. They asked your men to drive the vedmak away and burn his hut, and told them that they can have his ill-gotten gains.

{=th5MgyAZ}As you enter {TOWN_NAME}, one of your {ASERAI_TROOPS} approaches you. Many of his comrades are not used to the heat of the desert, he says. They march after drinking wine through the evening but are not careful to properly take water throughout the day, as the sun beats down on them. He has seen men collapse and die from such carelessness and ignorance.
{=trfafbJW}Third-Party Arbitration
{=u514BSH6}Tell them that you will not reward deceit
{=uD05twgi}Tell your men to ignore the superstitions of villagers, and press on.
{=uD8su80f}Tell them that you need the money for other purposes.
{=uJYOhEx8}Commend him, but tell him to stick with his comrades
{=uTsdJCSU}Besiegers' Blues

{=uXendo01}It was a hard-fought battle, and among your fallen is a young good-natured {TROOP_TYPE} who kept his comrades' spirits up during hard times. Your men’s faces are grim as they go out to collect the wounded of both sides. You can tell that, if they have their way, not many injured enemies will be brought back to your camp still alive as prisoners.
{=uppCchb0}Let them marry. Love must triumph over a father's pride
{=uqB1fKFY}Conflict Over Commons

{=vPNDzUAF}You strike up a conversation with a trader in town, who is desperate for news of the wars. When you tell him about the looting of {VILLAGE_NAME}, he makes a proposition. The price of grain will almost certainly rise, and he intends to buy up food now to sell it later when the hunger hits. He needs money, and he will sell you {OTHER_GOOD} at far below their market value - 1000 denars. He asks you also to keep this information to yourself.

{=vaez5WXH}As you leave town, you see a much larger number of beggars gathered than you would expect. Some of their limps look unconvincing. Your reputation for compassion and generosity may have gotten around.
{=vzA2ZJog}Pay, but say for all to hear that selective application of obscure laws is little better than theft.
{=vzFoybv0}Tell your party that, if this is true, then men are free to choose their own purpose in this world - and anyone who stands with you should make his purpose to help those in need.
{=vzOfEiKx}Wait briefly in the lee of a dune until the wind eases up, then press cautiously ahead
{=w3a39PVT}Give them an extra week's pay as a bonus, telling them they deserve far more but it is all you can afford.
{=wIakrAb}Explain to him that you cannot help.
{=wJ3Nh230}A breach is not worth the losses.
{=wLozeWS9}Ennoble a fighter
{=wcbbBjcD}Let it be

{=wlVCpQHS}Have them split it.
{=wnvUsbSs}Seize the land as your own, attracting desperate peasants from surrounding districts with exploitative sharecropping agreements
{=xEktDm2z}Job Offer

{=xH4KUzVS}As you leave town, you notice one of your horses has a swollen head and a bloody nose. You recognize this disease. It can spread to your men, and not only this animal is at risk but every other animal that drank from the same trough.
{=xJ0FKCtA}Let the villagers take the deer, even though your men scoff at your superstition
{=xSoKTeLL}Allow your men to collect some berries from the bushes
{=xYjLaJxA}Water supplies
{=xYuNxo3v}Let your men have some fun, but tell them to watch their purses and stay out of fights
{=xcPJPtaT}Demand the land for yourself.
{=xhuGmF9r}That the force of the blade lies only in the hand that wields it.
{=xoH5LaY0}Harangue your men for their barbarism, tell them to honor rather than mock their fallen foes.
{=xxVE2bw1}Improve the road, but charge no tolls
{=y0Ior5zV}If they are ripe why aren't they are already eaten by animals or collected? They might be poisonous. Avoid them

{=yJMpjiP7}As you set out again after the battle, you feel a few scattered drops of rain. Then there is a rush of wind, and a wall of dust engulfs you. The blowing grains sting your face, and you can see but a few arms' lengths ahead. You know that it is a simple matter for men to get lost in the notorious sandstorms of the Nahhas, only to be found later dead of thirst or buried in a dune.
{=yMoBOgxx}"You tell me," you say, with a mad laugh, as you deal him a slice that draws blood.

{=yXXbY1bb}You lie down for a well-deserved nap, but you slip into an uneasy dream. You are sailing on a wind-tossed sea. A wave crashes on your bow, sending spray across the decks. You look closely, and see that it is not water but blood sloshing around across your feet. You stare out into the sea, and the breakers take on the forms of men you have slain in battle.
{=ybnqAVbP}Force the afflicted to shave every strand of their hair and beard
{=yfsqkUcb}Tell the townspeople that Heaven wishes to test their compassion, and that they should treat the lepers with kindness.
{=ywaqOBG6}Give some draught animal to him so that he can continue on his way.
{=z0yA6wmV}Force your soldier to repay the loan with full interest
{=z15Ux7sh}Write truthfully that you don't know much about the bearer of the letter, but he comes from good family.

{=z4RgNBkq}On your way out of the village, a delegation led by the elder approaches you. They point to a {TROOP_TYPE} in your ranks - a good warrior, but none too outgoing. They say he used to farm in this village, but fled after he killed his neighbor in a quarrel over boundary stones. The accused snaps back with a sudden vehemence - his victim was a cheat, and deserved what he got. Under the law, murder requires the death penalty, though custom allows blood money to be paid instead.

{=zEPpgYaf}Reading won't help a farmboy plough, but might goad him to do foolish things that get him killed
{=zGVNqFnh}Buy vials of ointment for every member of your party, at the risk of looking gullible.
{=zM2vbhrt}Sit down with them and negotiate a mutual understanding.
{=zQ2rtAQE}Hunter's Paradise
{=zcMJEpHC}Don't get involved
{=zdPb0vtU}Treat the sick and make no additional demands on your men, trusting in luck to see you through this.

IL_4298: ldstr          {=ePstZcmu}Accept the recruits. The first chance you get, find fault with their gear and give them a sound thrashing, so they'll know to mend their ways.
IL_42e7: ldstr          {=Dogg1b9a}Take the recruits. Try not to be too hard on them at first, even though they'll probably corrode your party's discipline.
IL_4345: ldstr          {=EIbmlJRP}Tell the elder he'll need to find some other way to handle his troublemakers.

IL_4361: ldstr          {=FPnUWAj1}After the battle, one of your {TROOPS} from your party approaches you, dreamed of riding with your cavalry as a {NOBLE_TIER}. He has the money to buy his own horse, and he certainly distinguished himself in the fight. You know however that this will go down badly - with the high-born cavalry, who prefer to mingle with their own class, but probably even more so with his comrades, who will think he scorns them.

IL_437f: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_44c2: ldstr          {=uJYOhEx8}Commend him, but tell him to stick with his comrades

IL_4505: ldstr          {=BG8Ph5La}As you leave {VILLAGE_NAME}, a woman approaches you and grasps your horse's halter. Among your prisoners is her son, she says. You captured him when he was part of a gang of bandits, but she tells you tearfully that he is a good boy who fell in with bad company. She swears she'll ensure that he doesn't stray again from the correct path.

IL_4535: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_4590: ldstr          {=9yrWWbHF}Tell the woman that her son shall face the same penalties as any other bandit you caught
IL_45c5: ldstr          {=6sAI5uOm}Tell the village that they must pay the lad's ransom, so that he will know there is no profit in banditry

IL_464b: ldstr          {=VauaVUNS}You notice a footpath leading through your estate which could be quickly improved to be used by wagons and be a shortcut between the main trade roads. You could charge tolls and turn it into a turnpike, though the locals would resent the increased traffic and fees on their customary route.

IL_467c: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4682: ldstr          {=aF4Q5TJc}Widen the road for wagons but charge tolls to use it
IL_470c: ldstr          {=xxVE2bw1}Improve the road, but charge no tolls

IL_47db: ldstr          {=cRMxKTa8}Several freeholding farmers in your fief have fallen into debt through what appears to be a combination of bad luck and risky investments - a plough horse that died, a crop ruined by frost. They are unable to pay their taxes, and ask for a reprieve for several years.

IL_480c: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4812: ldstr          {=OM6tkdD7}You know an opportunity when you see it. Seize their lands. They can farm as your tenants
IL_4882: ldstr          {=jeWayyGY}A reprieve is fine, but you tack on a bit of interest so that you're not overwhelmed with hard luck stories
IL_48a6: ldstr          {=WHWokYrT}Call in a favor with a moneylender in town to reduce their debts so they can pay their taxes
IL_48f1: ldstr          {=3QobDImA}Help them get back on their feet, even if some will call say that you are too trusting

IL_495e: ldstr          {=lfJ6OHgX}The village has seen an unexpected rise in pregnancies. Some of your villagers ask your permission to hold a festival in honor of Agalea, protectress of motherhood. Agalea has never been recognized as a saint by the imperial Senate, and many consider her veneration to be a primitive Palaic holder. Her festivals tend to be rather raucous, befitting the theme of fertility, and also rather expensive. It would certainly set tongues wagging in the district. Do you grant permission?

IL_498f: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4995: ldstr          {=EFUNx0cv}A vat of wine for you to dance in honor of the lady Agalea!
IL_4a89: ldstr          {=NWNIVZF0}Give the villagers a stern lecture on the importance of sound doctrine and lawful worship
IL_4b25: ldstr          {=J9BsFeSS}Tell the villagers to keep things discrete

IL_4b99: ldstr          {=2KaXj3Qa}The depredations of the {NEARBY_ENEMY_FACTION} has driven many farmers from their homes. Those who have land usually return to it, but many of the poorer are seeking a new place to live. You speak to a few encamped on the outskirts of your village. There is no land for them. They seem eager to work as tenants, but there is always a possibility of tensions with the more established village families.

IL_4bca: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4bd0: ldstr          {=8JqCDWRd}Welcome them, and give them a donation to purchase small plots of land.
IL_4c80: ldstr          {=U4UJn9X4}Let them stay. Tell both newcomers and longtime residents to get along, and hope for the best.
IL_4cf3: ldstr          {=o4aQ2UEL}Tell them to make their homes someplace else.

IL_4d21: ldstr          {=U4Ybz08z}A desperate band of nomads has arrived at your village, seeking a place to settle down. Their herds were ravaged by an epidemic, they say, and they are ready to take up farming or work as laborers. Otherwise, they must starve or give themselves to another tribe as servants. The villagers are skeptical. Nomads are too lazy to be farmers, they say, preferring horse theft and feuds.

IL_4d52: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4d58: ldstr          {=iSZCkpt3}Welcome them with open arms and a small donation to buy plots of land for their homes
IL_4e08: ldstr          {=taVbaFFW}Sternly instruct them to respect the traditions of settled life, even though the cold welcome might scare some away
IL_4e69: ldstr          {=jUlHTiSU}Agree with the villagers that nomads are more trouble than they are worth.

IL_4e97: ldstr          {=raLLq10c}Grazing land has grown scarce near {TOWN_OR_CASTLE_NAME}, and a heath between {POORER_VILLAGE} and {RICHER_VILLAGE}, covered with thistle and formerly of little value, has become a point of contention. {POORER_VILLAGE} claims that they have been taking goats there for generations, but {RICHER_VILLAGE} has produced a document showing legal title.

IL_4ec8: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4ece: ldstr          {=cVzpV96W}The laws of the realm are clear: no matter how many years go by, the original owner retains the land unless it is legally sold or transferred.
IL_4f4c: ldstr          {=3zEtGAII}You agree with the ancient Palaic principle: the lands belong to the spirits of the earth, not to humans, and go to those who make the best use of them.
IL_5028: ldstr          {=YWZFOX4S}Let them know that your decision is for sale at a price

IL_50d7: ldstr          {=jGafCYMe}Villagers from your fief of {VILLAGE} have started going to a marsh on the road to {VILLAGE2} to gather reeds for baskets, supplementing their earnings. Hunters from {VILLAGE2}, owned by {LORD.NAME}, say they've been disturbing the local waterfowl. Neither of you has title to the marsh, but {VILLAGE2} says that its people started going there first. Your tenants say it's not their problem if they've figured out a better way to make use of the resources.

IL_50f5: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_50fb: ldstr          {=8gTYsXZM}Continue to send your reed gatherers there, and have them bring staves and slings to defend their rights
IL_519f: ldstr          {=0xiAZr96}Tell {NOBLE.NAME} that your people will get their reeds elsewhere and stop frightening off the game.

IL_521c: ldstr          {=2OQlwt7x}Villagers say that a wanderer has recently arrived and offered to teach their children to read. He is not only well-educated, but he has a gift for holding the attention of restless 10-year-olds. However, he seems to have spent time with one of the rebel bands that were common around here ten years back, and occasionally speaks of a coming reign of justice brought by Heaven, in a way that doesn't seem like one of his ironic jokes.

IL_524d: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5253: ldstr          {=Wuga4ZqG}Let him stay. It's good for children to read, and it's not like they take their elders seriously anyway
IL_52cd: ldstr          {=zEPpgYaf}Reading won't help a farmboy plough, but might goad him to do foolish things that get him killed
IL_52f0: ldstr          {=3OerG5Ik}Take the teacher aside, and tell him the elder will pay him a handsome stipend that will stop abruptly if he breathes a word about politics or theology.

IL_5374: ldstr          {=eQz8b4TH}The village is buzzing with a poorly kept secret. Following a rare but fierce rainstorm in the dry hills, fishermen have begun to find small flakes of gold in a local stream. If word gets out, there will be a huge influx of fortune-seekers into the area. The gold will last a few months, and it's not clear how much of it will benefit the village or its owner.

IL_53a5: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_53ab: ldstr          {=mEqk8UCG}This region could use more people. Let word get out.
IL_5451: ldstr          {=aNGQJJkM}As liege of the village, the gold belongs to you. Post guards along the river to stop unauthorized prospecting
IL_54cd: ldstr          {=cECwyvjY}Encourage the villagers to mine it stealthily, ensuring their cooperation by allowing them to keep it
IL_5551: ldstr          {=7q53TLg7}Wages of war and diseases

IL_5556: ldstr          {=FZXYHC7s}Between the wars and an epidemic, the villages near {FIEF_NAME} are experiencing a shortage of people, especially young men. Fields are going fallow for lack of hands to plough them, especially those cleared only in recent generations where the title is in dispute. As liege, you can redistribute this unused land, but you will need to find labor.

IL_5587: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_558d: ldstr          {=wnvUsbSs}Seize the land as your own, attracting desperate peasants from surrounding districts with exploitative sharecropping agreements
IL_5617: ldstr          {=8jCcqBSV}Distribute the land to some of your veterans as a reward for their service
IL_56b2: ldstr          {=QSEZfwVk}Distribute money to the region's farmers so they can hire agricultural laborers or provide attractive dowries for their daughters

IL_5765: ldstr          {=evcKUaab}An early thaw and a warm spring has ensured a bumper crop, which the prayers of the villagers and the efforts of the local cats have protected from rats and birds. Such bounties occur rarely. What will you do?

IL_5796: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_579c: ldstr          {=HT1mQuCI}Feast! Thank Heaven and the spirits of the land, and make merry
IL_5867: ldstr          {=c5vobNeb}Encourage the farmers to sell the crops and make much-needed improvements to irrigation and roads
IL_58b6: ldstr          {=ZaBiC5XV}Go through your accounts to see who might owe you back taxes

IL_5911: ldstr          {=yXXbY1bb}You lie down for a well-deserved nap, but you slip into an uneasy dream. You are sailing on a wind-tossed sea. A wave crashes on your bow, sending spray across the decks. You look closely, and see that it is not water but blood sloshing around across your feet. You stare out into the sea, and the breakers take on the forms of men you have slain in battle.

IL_5946: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_594c: ldstr          {=sxrBpIUk}Have I killed without good reason? Heaven wishes me to repent! I shall choose the peaceful path. When there is one, that is...
IL_5985: ldstr          {=a0MWe8GO}To where do we sail on this sea of blood? To glory, that is where!
IL_59bd: ldstr          {=B1cyEaQA}Dreams are but a temporary madness. Heaven does not speak to us in this way.

IL_59eb: ldstr          {=5OuDl2Po}As you come into town, the merchant {MERCHANT_NAME} makes you an offer. Local merchants are on edge awaiting an incoming caravan from {PLACE}. If you claim that you found its wreckage, looted by bandits, the prices of goods would rise considerably. He offers to pay you 1000 denars, in addition to whatever extra you can make by selling your own wares once the prices rise.

IL_5a0d: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5a13: ldstr          {=SLASexva}Accept, but leave enough room for doubt in your account that it won't look too bad if the caravan turns up.
IL_5ad2: ldstr          {=EyHD7gjy}Say you'll swear up and down that you saw the wreckage, damaging your reputation, but demand 2000 denars instead.
IL_5b97: ldstr          {=aMMxVIpa}Erupt in anger for all to see, and curse {MERCHANT} for taking you for a base liar.
IL_5c1c: ldstr          {=UbZMlyk6}Take a pass on the matter.

IL_5c38: ldstr          {=H7Co1wqC}Two of your {NOBLE_TIER} have lately been causing a stir in the camp with their irreverent religious preaching. They propound that this world is a illusion, created by a being called the Demiurge for its own amusement, and humans are but game-pieces. You think this may be the Marcorionist doctrine, declared heretical by the imperial Senate some years ago. It is clearly disturbing your more traditional-minded troops and is probably also not good for your party's reputation.

IL_5c56: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5c5c: ldstr          {=WyuxrGqC}Tell them, in a towering fury, that if they do not wish to be burned then they had best either leave your party or cease this sacrilege
IL_5cb9: ldstr          {=4WZ5CWm8}Take them aside and tell them that while nihilism is fine for a boozy salon in {TOWN_NAME}, it's a bit much for men who must every day put their lives on the line.

IL_5d15: ldstr          {=vzFoybv0}Tell your party that, if this is true, then men are free to choose their own purpose in this world - and anyone who stands with you should make his purpose to help those in need.
IL_5d48: ldstr          {=e07rQCcq}Tell the men that this is splendid news for brave men like themselves, as surely nothing would amuse the Demiurge more than a good fight.

IL_5dab: ldstr          {=vPNDzUAF}You strike up a conversation with a trader in town, who is desperate for news of the wars. When you tell him about the looting of {VILLAGE_NAME}, he makes a proposition. The price of grain will almost certainly rise, and he intends to buy up food now to sell it later when the hunger hits. He needs money, and he will sell you {OTHER_GOOD} at far below their market value - 1000 denars. He asks you also to keep this information to yourself.

IL_5dc9: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5dcf: ldstr          {=aUui6FYp}All's fair in trade and war. You accept the deal.
IL_5e52: ldstr          {=2xvqOUJh}Tell him quietly that you will not profit off of the misery of others.
IL_5e75: ldstr          {=hnMUxRyt}Denounce him angrily in public as a food hoarder for all to hear, so that word gets around of your compassion and mercy.

IL_5ec8: ldstr          {=nyZpbVbv}Your men are very proud of their leader - perhaps too proud. Every time they go into town, they spread exaggerated tales of your recklessness in battle. You imagine that this could win you a few admiring recruits, but more and more you've caught a look that suggests fear or distrust, as though you're a wild animal or a demon.

IL_5ef8: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5efe: ldstr          {=bbH4PqtD}Let the tales spread! Sanity and caution do not inspire legend
IL_5f5f: ldstr          {=Qbdym8vH}In a towering rage, tell your men that you will not tolerate lies of any sort.
IL_5f94: ldstr          {=EzpB6hJG}Try to play down the image of a madman by being as friendly as possible on your next visit to town.

IL_5fd4: ldstr          {=IxgJotDk}At first this siege gave your men a welcome respite from the hardships of the march, but now inactivity and boredom has started to take a toll. Even dice and gossip have lost their charms, and you're starting to see quarrels and lapses in discipline.

IL_6009: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_600f: ldstr          {=LUap9uP0}Drill your men for the upcoming assault, even though the ever-present risk of injury might put several out of commission when they're needed most.

IL_6048: ldstr          {=GTPPtara}March about the camp, searching for specks of rust on swords or sentries who aren't fully attentive to their watch. Give any violators hard, pointless tasks to teach them to keep their standards up.
IL_6095: ldstr          {=bp8kKb1A}Let the men enjoy their rest.

IL_60d3: ldstr          {=YCPF4qyz}You are approached by a pair of Skolderbroda. They are anxious to fight for you and ask only that you pay them a token sum. They say you that a warlord like you deserves the services of men such as themselves - praise to you, but a slight to the rest of your party. One of your troops tells you that he's sure that these men must have broken their vows to their company, or why else would they be so eager to join you?

IL_6103: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6109: ldstr          {=Kqr9pVCU}Take them into your company. Your troops will need to bear any insult.
IL_615c: ldstr          {=78VrrDRM}Tell them that you believe them to be oathbreakers, and as such have no place in your ranks.
IL_617f: ldstr          {=1b9oYu6v}Tell them they can join you and be as arrogant as they like - so long as they beat one of your men in a duel to first blood.

IL_620b: ldstr          {=K8DJmY4L}Several of your {TROOP_TYPE} have an idea for the next battle. They suggest that they be hidden in a supply wagon and left for the enemy to discover and drag into camp, whereupon they will leap out and wreak havoc. They are very proud of their scheme, even though you can think of half a dozen reasons it won't work.

IL_6228: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_622e: ldstr          {=X68PZrYv}Tell them that every people in Calradia has its own legend about warriors concealed in unlikely places, and you can't imagine them getting away with it.
IL_6264: ldstr          {=Gsazqfhj}Let them test their plan. Buy a hide, sew the men into it with their weapons, and gather the company to watch in amusement as they struggle to free themselves.
IL_62c9: ldstr          {=YhxsQjGM}Nod quickly as though you weren't really listening and move on to some other task.

IL_62f7: ldstr          {=42bGMh4X}Your men were not expecting to spend so much time in the desert. They complain that baggage that they might gladly carry themselves in normal times becomes a crushing burden when the blazing sun is high in the sky. They have located a number of pack animals in the markets and ask you to buy them to lighten their own loads.

IL_6327: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_632d: ldstr          {=ACzeec4e}Agree to purchase the camels.
IL_63c3: ldstr          {=uD8su80f}Tell them that you need the money for other purposes.

IL_674d: ldstr          {=QEP3ntdb}Merchants are savvy to most attempts to pass off most types of shoddy goods as top quality, but one of your {TROOP.NAME} knows a few tricks that aren't in the usual rogue's repetoire.
